about: Touched-path → test-suite map, read by `botq test-map`. The acceptance gate derives every landed job's touched paths from its own diff and requires the commands mapped here green — independent of the job's brief. First matching rule wins: specific rules above broad ones. `tests: []` means CONSCIOUSLY untested and must carry its why. An unmapped path fails the resolver loud. Commands run from the repo root; lint completeness with `botq test-map --check`.

rules.why: editing the map re-lints its own completeness over every tracked file

the authenticated BLE credential hop spans the existing binary, its static initramfs build and the BlueZ closure in the boot image; all three artifacts must build and the protocol plus existing UDP patch must remain green
the single pinned nixpkgs every nix build in the repo imports — changing it must still build both the static agent and the stick image

the qemu/OVMF Secure-Boot boot harness and the in-VM hwsim rig it bakes in — a full run needs OVMF firmware, KVM and a booted VM, so the gate checks syntax only; run `bash boot/run-boot.sh` (EGDOD_BOOT_LINK=wired|station|ap|ble) manually to exercise them
BlueZ's controller emulator, built from the pinned source for the ble boot mode's virtual air; the gate proves it still builds, the boot run exercises it
the busybox-sh DHCP lease-apply script baked into the initramfs — a full exercise needs a booted VM and a DHCP server, so the gate checks syntax only

the guarded physical-stick writer and the two steps it composes — networks.sh reads the writing host's wireless profile as root, write-stick.sh writes a real block device — so the gate checks syntax only; bake.sh is exercised by every run-boot.sh link proof
the live proof harness — a full run needs a controller, sudo netns and the public relay, so the gate checks syntax only; run `nix-shell --run './demo.sh'` manually when touching it
the pinned dev environment — every cargo command below runs inside it, so a break fails those loudly

the vendored noq-udp patch, the [patch.crates-io] wiring and the lockfile exist for the static musl agent (SPEC property 4, egdod#3) — so besides both native suites, the host build and the cross build must still produce a binary; nix caches them by input hash
the package's own suite; musl-specific breakage lives in libc-facing deps (covered by the vendor rule), not here
